                                      EXECUTIVE ORDER


BY THE GOVERNOR:


                 STATE OF EMERGENCY FOR THE PASSING OF PRESIDENT CARTER


   WHEREAS: The nation and our state lost a great leader with the passing of President James
            Earl Carter, Jr. on December 29, 2024; and

   WHEREAS: President Carter’s final farewell will attract visitors, domestically and
            internationally, wishing to pay their respects and mourn with other likeminded
            individuals; and

   WHEREAS: President Carter’s hometown of Plains, Georgia is a rural community and the
            number of expected visitors during President Carter’s final farewell will exceed the
            management capacity of the local governments; and

   WHEREAS: The influx of persons to Plains, Georgia, and the surrounding communities, if not
            carefully curated with additional transportation and public safety personnel, will
            impact the citizens of Georgia living in or traveling through the area; and

   WHEREAS: Code Section 38-3-51 vests the Governor with the authority to issue orders, rules,
            and regulations to protect the safety and welfare of the public in certain situations.

                NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTION 38-3-51, AND THE AUTHORITY
                VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

   ORDERED:     That all resources of the state be made available to assist with the final farewell and
                interment of President Carter.

                IT IS FURTHER

   ORDERED:     That a State of Emergency exists in Sumter County for the limited purpose of
                allowing state resources to meet the personnel and logistical challenges presented
                in executing President Carter’s final farewell and interment.
           IT IS FURTHER

ORDERED:   That the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency activate
           the State Operations Center to coordinate all state assets assisting with the final
           farewell and interment of President Carter.

           IT IS FURTHER

ORDERED:   That the State of Emergency portion of this Executive Order shall be valid for a
           period of fourteen (14) days, beginning on December 29, 2024, and ending at 11:59
           pm on January 12, 2025.

           This 29th day of December 2024.

                             EXECUTIVE ORDER


BY THE GOVERNOR:


                   FLAGS ON ALL STATE BUILDINGS AND GROUNDS
                       ORDERED LOWERED TO HALF-STAFF


     WHEREAS:      Today we celebrate the life of the late James E. “Jimmy” Carter, Jr.,
                   former Governor of Georgia, and President of the United States from
                   1977 to 1981; and

     WHEREAS:      A man from humble roots, Jimmy Carter was born in Plains, Georgia,
                   as the oldest sibling of three children to James and Bessie Carter,
                   owners of a local peanut farm, warehouse, and store in the
                   surrounding community; and

     WHEREAS:      As a young man, Jimmy Carter was admitted to the Naval Academy
                   in Annapolis, Maryland, where he excelled academically and
                   eventually earned his bachelor’s degree. He subsequently served
                   seven years as a naval officer, rising to the rank of Lieutenant; and

     WHEREAS:      After his father’s death, Carter resigned his commission as an officer
                   in the armed forces to return to his childhood home and manage the
                   family business, becoming a successful peanut farmer in South
                   Georgia and well-respected member of his community and church;
                   and

     WHEREAS:      His desire to serve others and love of politics inspired Jimmy Carter
                   to successfully run for state office as a two-term Georgia State
                   Senator; and

     WHEREAS:      On January 12, 1971, Jimmy Carter was sworn in as the 76th Governor
                   of the state of Georgia. During his gubernatorial tenure, Carter was
                   a fierce advocate for civil rights, education reform, and more efficient
                   government processes; and
WHEREAS:   As the first Georgia native to ever serve in the nation’s highest
           political office, Jimmy Carter became the 39th President of the United
           States on January 20, 1977; and

WHEREAS:   In 1982, Jimmy Carter opened the Carter Center in Atlanta, Georgia
           to advance international human rights, promote democracy, and
           improve health; and

WHEREAS:   Across the globe, former President Jimmy Carter is widely respected
           for his work in human rights and health education in developing
           countries, and he was awarded with the Nobel Peace Prize in 2002
           for his efforts as a world-renowned humanitarian and
           philanthropist; and

WHEREAS:   On this day, December 29, 2024, the date of his death, we honor the
           memory of Georgia native, Jimmy Carter, as a revered community
           activist, veteran, statesman, author, former Governor of Georgia, and
           former President of the United States.

           NOW, THEREFORE, IN HONOR OF FORMER PRESIDENT OF THE
           UNITED STATES OF AMERICA JIMMY CARTER, AND PURSUANT TO
           THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF
           GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

ORDERED:   That, pursuant to 4 U.S.C. Chapter 1, Section 7, subsection (m), the
           flag of the United States and the flag of the State of Georgia should
           be flown at half-staff on all state buildings and grounds for thirty
           days from December 29, 2024, the day of his death, until sunset on
           January 28, 2025.

           This 29th day of December 2024.

BY THE GOVERNOR:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

ORDERED:

The quality of our system of administering justice is determined by the
quality of the judicial officers elected and appointed to serve within our
judicial system; and

It is the responsibility and the duty of the Governor under Ga. Const. art.
VI, § 7, { II] to appoint duly qualified persons to fill vacancies in the courts
arising during the Governor’s term of office; and

It is essential that the Governor fills judicial vacancies with men and women
of the highest capacity whom by temperament, ability and integrity will
freely, impartially, and independently interpret the law and administer
justice; and

Judicial candidates demonstrating excellence should be drawn from a
cross-section of our community, reflecting the diversity of our citizenry; and

A non-partisan, non-political judicial nominating commission composed of
outstanding lawyers and laypersons in aid to the discretion reposed in the
Governor, drawn from all quarters of the State and a cross-section of its
diverse population best ensures the highest quality of judicial
appointments.

NOW, THEREFORE, BY VIRTUE OF THE POWER VESTED IN ME AS
GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That there is created the Judicial Nominating Commission for the State of
Georgia. The Commission shall make nominations to fill vacancies on all
courts of record in the State. The Commission created by this order shall
supersede Executive Order 10.26.21.01.

IT IS FURTHER

That the Commission shall consist of members that have demonstrable
knowledge of the judicial system and experience in the needs and operation

ORDERED:

ORDERED:

ORDERED:

ORDERED:

ORDERED:

of Georgia courts. Members who are members of the Bar shall have
appropriate experience relevant with the courts as former judges, former
magistrates, trial counsel, government counsel, or corporate counsel and
shall be members of the State Bar of Georgia in good standing. Members
who are not members of the Bar shall be familiar with the attributes that
best qualify a person for appointment as a judicial officer.

IT IS FURTHER

That the Georgia Judicial Nominating Commission shall consist of
members appointed by the Governor to serve at the pleasure of the
Governor. All members shall be residents of the State of Georgia.
Appointments shall be made with a view toward equitable geographic
representation and shall reflect the diversity of the State’s citizenry.

IT IS FURTHER

That in the event of a judicial vacancy, the Commission shall advertise the
vacancy and elicit applications of qualified persons to fill the vacancy; meet
and consider persons for submission as nominees according to merit and
law and shall recommend to the Governor individuals which it finds
qualified for each judiciary vacancy.

ITIS FURTHER

That all written communications by the Commission or any member with
any applicant or with any person or entity concerning an applicant shall be
limited to Commission stationery. No law firm or law practice letterhead
stationery shall be used in connection with any such communication.

ITIS FURTHER

That the members of the State Bar of Georgia shall at all times act in
accordance with professional and ethical standards set forth by the Bar. All
members shall at all times act according to the highest professional and
ethical standards.

IT IS FURTHER

That Mark Middleton, Esq., Vincent Russo, Esq., and the Honorable Shawn
LaGrua are appointed as Co-Chairs of the Commission to serve at the
pleasure of the Governor. Vincent Russo will be responsible for the record
keeping and operation of the commission.

                                     EXECUTIVE ORDER


BY THE GOVERNOR:

                           FLAGS ON STATE BUILDINGS AND GROUNDS
                              ORDERED LOWERED TO HALF-STAFF

   WHEREAS: Mr. Bruce Thompson, Georgia’s Commissioner of Labor, passed away on
            November 24, 2024; and

   WHEREAS: Commissioner Thompson honorably served our country for six years within the
            Tank/Armored Division of the U.S. Army National Guard; and

   WHEREAS: Commissioner Thompson represented the 14th district in the Georgia State Senate
            from December 2013 until January 2023 when he took office as Commissioner of
            Labor; and

   WHEREAS: As Georgia’s tenth Commissioner of Labor, Bruce Thompson used his work ethic,
            integrity, and legislative experience to serve Georgia’s workers and employers by
            leading an agency focused on transparency, responsiveness, and fiscal
            responsibility; and

   WHEREAS: It is fitting and proper to remember and honor Bruce Thompson’s service to the
            State of Georgia by lowering flags on all State buildings and grounds to half-staff.

                NOW, THEREFORE, IN HONOR OF AND AS A MARK OF RESPECT FOR THE
                MEMORY OF BRUCE THOMPSON, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME
                AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

   ORDERED:     That the flag of the United States and the flag of the State of Georgia be flown at
                half-staff on all State buildings and grounds on Saturday, November 30, 2024, the
                day of Commissioner Bruce Thompson’s interment.

                This 29th day of November 2024.

and property of the people; and

REGARDING FAIRNESS TO GEORGIA’S STUDENT-ATHLETES IN COMPENSATION FOR

WHEREAS:

THEIR NAME, IMAGE, AND LIKENESS

The State of Georgia boasts postsecondary educational institutions and
intercollegiate student-athletes excelling at the highest level of
intercollegiate athletics; and

The National Collegiate Athletic Association (the “NCAA”) and certain
athletic conferences have entered into a proposed settlement agreement
(the “Settlement”) in In re College Athlete NIL Litigation, No. 4:20-cv-
03919-CW (N.D. Cal.) (“the Litigation”), which, if approved, would permit
postsecondary institutions to provide direct compensation to student-
athletes for the use of such student-athletes name, image of likeness

(“NIL”); and

Until the Settlement is approved and effective, legislative and executive
actions across the country create a patchwork of inconsistent rules
regulating intercollegiate athletics; and

Student-athletes in the State of Georgia should compete on a level playing
field and not forgo compensation available to student-athletes in other
states while the Settlement is pending.

NOW, THEREFORE, BY THE POWER VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE
STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That neither the NCAA, an athletic conference, nor any other organization
with authority over intercollegiate athletics shall take any adverse action
against a postsecondary educational institution in the State of Georgia for
such institution facilitating compensation, offering compensation, or
compensating an intercollegiate student-athlete for the use of such student-

ORDERED:

athlete’s NIL; provided, however, that no postsecondary educational
institution shall use funds allocated by the State of Georgia for such
compensation,

IT IS FURTHER

That the provisions of this Order shall become effective upon signature and
shall remain in effect until the earlier of:

1. The effective date of any federal law enacted after the date of this Order
regulating the rights of student-athletes to receive compensation for the
use of their NIL; or

2. The effective date of any settlement related to the Litigation.

Upon the earlier of one of these events, this Order shall be rendered null
and without effect.

It is fitting and proper to recognize the injured and remember those who lost their
lives—Mr. Richard Aspinwall, 39; Ms. Christina Irimie, 53; Mr. Christian Angulo,
14; and Mr. Mason Schermerhorn, 14—by lowering the flags on all State buildings
and grounds throughout Georgia to half-staff.

NOW, THEREFORE, AS A MARK OF RESPECT FOR THOSE AFFECTED BY THIS
TERRIBLE TRAGEDY, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS
GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That the flag of the United States and the flag of the State of Georgia shall be flown
at half-staff on all State buildings and grounds from this date until sunset on the
date of the final victim’s interment.

IT IS FURTHER

That the Office of the Governor may continue to issue guidance on the effective

date of this Order as needed through communication media, including social
media, without the need for further Executive Orders.

STATE OF EMERGENCY FOR TROPICAL DEPRESSION 4

Tropical Depression 4 is forecasted to travel into the eastern Gulf of
Mexico and become Tropical Storm Debby this evening, Saturday,
August 3, 2024, or early on Sunday, August 4, 2024; and

The storm is forecasted to make landfall in the early morning on
Monday, August 5, 2024, along areas of the Florida gulf coast and
portions of the Florida panhandle and is projected to travel
northwest affecting areas in south central Georgia and southeast
coastal Georgia; and

The National Hurricane Center forecasts that this storm may
produce heavy rainfall, storm surge, and flooding in the State of
Georgia; and

This storm has the potential to produce severe impacts to citizens
throughout south central and southeast coastal Georgia; and

Preliminary reports from county emergency management agencies
and the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security
Agency indicate a need for assistance in the impacted counties; and

Assistance from the State of Georgia is necessary to provide for the
public's safety, protect public and private property, and maintain the
social and economic welfare of the State; and

The Federal Motor Carrier Safety regulations, 49 C.F.R. § 390, et
seq., limit the hours of operators of commercial motor vehicles may
drive; and

49 C.F.R. § 390.23 allows the Governor of a State to suspend these
rules and regulations for up to 30 days if the Governor determines
that an emergency condition exists; and

The Governor is vested with the emergency powers cited herein as
the Chief Executive of this State; and

regulations promulgated by the Governor" have the force and effect
of law; and

As Chief Executive, the Governor is tasked with protecting the
citizens of this State, including during a state of emergency; and

Code Section 38-3-51(c)(1) vests the Governor with the power to
enforce all laws, rules, and regulations relating to emergency
management and to assume direct operational control of all civil
forces and helpers in the state; and

Code Section 38-3-51(c)(4) vests the Governor with the power to
perform and exercise such other functions, powers, and duties as
may be deemed necessary to promote and secure the safety and
protection of the civilian population; and

In consultation with state emergency preparedness officials, I have
determined that the following actions are necessary and appropriate
to protect the health, safety, and welfare of Georgia's residents and
visitors.

38-3-51, AND THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE
STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That a State of Emergency exists in the State of Georgia due to the
potential negative impact of Tropical Depression 4.

On June 11, 2024, Mr. Marcello Banes, Chairman of the Newton County
Board of Commissioners, was indicted by the United States Attorney for the
Northern District of Georgia on one count of Money Laundering
Conspiracy, three counts of Transactional Money Laundering, one count of
Concealment Money Laundering, and one count of False Statements to a
Federal Agent; and

A certified copy of the indictment was transmitted to the Governor pursuant
to Code Section 45-5-6(b), and received on July 9, 2024; and

The fourteen-day period following receipt of the indictment as prescribed
by Code Section 45-5-6(e) has passed.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTION 45-5-6, AND THE
AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS
HEREBY

That Attorney General Christopher Carr, Clinton Johnson of the Dougherty
County Board of Commissioners, and Bruce Henry of the Jasper County
Board of Commissioners are hereby appointed as the review commission to
determine whether the above-mentioned indictment relates to and
adversely affects the administration of duties by Mr. Banes such that the
rights and interests of the public are adversely affected thereby, and to make
a written report to me within fourteen days with a recommendation as to
whether Mr. Banes should be suspended from office as required by Code

Section 45-5-6(c).

On June 3, 2024, Mr. Elvis Davis, a member of the Dodge County Board of
Education, was indicted on two counts of Child Molestation and two counts
of Sexual Contact by a Foster Parent in the first degree; and

A certified copy of the indictment was transmitted to the Governor pursuant
to Code Section 45-5-6(b), and received on June 6, 2024; and

An Executive Order was issued on June 24, 2024, appointing members to
the Review Commission to determine whether the indictment relates to and
adversely affects the administration of the Office of the Dodge County Board
of Education; and

By report dated July 1, 2024, the Review Commission found that the
indictment of Mr. Elvis Davis does relate to and does adversely affect the
administration of the Office of the Dodge County Board of Education, and
that the rights and interests of the public are adversely affected thereby; and
recommended that Mr. Elvis Davis be suspended from office pursuant to
the provisions of Code Section 45-5-6.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTION 45-5-6, AND THE
AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS
HEREBY

That Mr. Elvis Davis is hereby suspended from office immediately and
without further action pending the final disposition of the case or until the
expiration of his term of office, whichever occurs first, as provided in Code

Section 45-5-6(c).

BY THE GOVERNOR:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

I have been informed by officials of the Georgia Housing and Finance
Authority (the “Issuer”) that the Issuer desires to sell and issue up to
and including $250,000,000 of its single family mortgage bonds (the
“Bonds”) in order to provide monies to finance, in whole or in part,
newly originated mortgage loans on single family residential housing
units for eligible persons and families of low or moderate income in
the State of Georgia, to refund and redeem certain outstanding bonds
of the Issuer, to establish any necessary reserves, and to pay all or a
portion of the costs of sale and issuance of the Bonds; and

The Bonds will be issued by the Issuer, which is an instrumentality
of the State of Georgia; the mortgages purchased will finance
properties located entirely within the boundaries of the State of
Georgia; and

I am the chief elected executive officer of the State of Georgia; and

This Executive Order is intended solely to constitute the approval
required by Section 147(f) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as
amended; and

A hearing related to the proposed issuance of the Bonds, open to the
public, was held on August 31, 2023, for which due and reasonable
public notice was given in accordance with the provisions of law and
the procedures established therefor; and

Following such hearing, the Georgia Housing and Finance Authority
recommended that the issuance of the Bonds be approved and
requested this approval.

Now, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME
AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

ORDERED: That I approve the issuance of the Bonds by the Georgia Housing and
Finance Authority, solely for the purpose of satisfying the
requirements for such approval under Section 147(f) of the Internal
Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, and the regulations promulgated
thereunder, and for no other purpose.

IT Is FURTHER
ORDERED: That this Executive Order shall take effect immediately upon its

adoption and that the Executive Counsel of the Governor shall place
a public record of this Executive Order in the Executive Minutes.

On Memorial Day, Monday, May 27, 2024, Americans will once again join
together in honoring the brave men and women who served this great
nation and made the ultimate sacrifice in the name of freedom. As proud
Americans, we reflect on and value the courage of our fellow Georgians and
countrymen who represent the highest ideals of our nation as they carry our
flag into battle, knowing they may never return; and

On this Memorial Day, Georgians again honor and mourn the loss of United
States Army Reserve soldiers Staff Seargeant William Jerome Rivers, of
Carrollton, Georgia, Sergeant Breonna Alexsondria Moffett, of Savannah,
Georgia, and Sergeant Kennedy Landon Sanders, of Waycross, Georgia,
whose lives were tragically lost in the name of our freedom in a drone attack
at a base in Jordan on January 28, 2024; and

This day marks the time of year where we mourn the fallen and count our
blessings. This country would be nothing without those who gave their lives
to preserve liberty. Because of them, we are blessed to live in a free country
where the American dream is real-where our families can live, grow, and
prosper—all because of our soldiers’ willingness to put country above self.
For their acts of valor, we owe a debt that can never be repaid; and

For families across the United States, there are difficult emotions associated
with days like today. They represent great sadness and hope, grief and
celebration, conflict and peace. Although we cannot erase your pain, please
know that we will always stand by you. We will honor your loved ones’
sacrifice, We will permanently etch their names into our hearts and minds,
and we will lift you up in our thoughts and prayers; and

This Memorial Day, as we meet with friends and family, let us all pause and
remember the fallen. Let us pray for our veterans, the brave men and
women who currently serve in our Armed Forces, and their families.
Remember that these families serve our nation by supporting their loved
ones in uniform. We must pledge to act worthy of their sacrifices year-

and continue to serve.

DEFENSE OF OUR NATION, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS

ORDERED LOWERED TO HALF STAFF

Colonel Ralph Puckett, Jr., U.S. Army (retired), of Columbus, Georgia,
honorably served our country in the United States Army; and

Colonel Puckett was the last living person to receive the Medal of Honor for
heroism during the Korean War; and

Colonel Puckett was a decorated war hero having received two
Distinguished Service Crosses, two Silver Stars, five Purple Hearts, and two
Bronze Star Medals with the “V” device for valor; and

It is fitting and proper to recognize the service Colonel Puckett by lowering
the flags on the State Capitol building and in Muscogee County to half-staff.

NOw, THEREFORE, IN HONOR AND AS A MARK OF RESPECT FOR THE
MEMORY OF COLONEL RALPH PUCKETT, JR., PURSUANT TO THE
AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS
HEREBY

That the flag of the United States and the flag of the State of Georgia be
flown at half-staff on the State Capitol building and in Muscogee County on

Saturday, April 20, 2024, the day of the public ceremony to honor Colonel
Puckett.

This 18 day of April 2024.

various deeds and filed in the office of the Clerk of Superior Court of Taliaferro
County, and filed with the State Properties Commission Real Property Record as
Property BLLIP ID# 51525; and

Said Property is in the custody of the Department of Natural Resources and is
commonly known as A.H. Stephens State Park; and

The Property is improved with a structure identified as the “Group Shelter” (BLLIP
ID #12665) being approximately 1,865 square feet (hereinafter, collectively called,
the “Structure”), as shown in the aerial photograph and map attached hereto as
Exhibit “A”; and

Said Structure was condemned for structural integrity as the cost to repair and
bring up to ADA compliance was determined to cost more than it is worth; and

The Office of the State Archaeologist determined the Structure to be historic, and
Photographic Permanent Archival Record was completed, reviewed and approved
by Historic Preservation Division and will not impact the Georgia/National
Register of Historic Places; and

By resolution dated October 24, 2023, the Board of Natural Resources requested
authority to demolish the Structure.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS
GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

The Department of Natural Resources is authorized and directed to provide for the
razing, demolition, and disposal of said Structure under the terms and conditions
which are deemed to be in the best interest of the State of Georgia, in accordance with
applicable laws, policies, and procedures, including any requirements under O.C.G.A
12-3-55 regarding historic properties that may pertain to the Structure.

EXECUTIVE ORDER APPROVING THE
ISSUANCE OF PRIVATE ACTIVITY BONDS

I, as Governor of the State of Georgia, have been informed by officials of the
Private Colleges and Universities Authority (the “Authority”) that the
Authority on January 11, 2024, approved the application (the
“Application”) of The Corporation of Mercer University, a nonprofit
corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of Georgia
(“Mercer”), with respect to a plan of the issuance of Private Colleges and
Universities Authority Revenue Bonds (Mercer University Project), Series
2024 (the “Series 2024 Bonds’), to be issued in an aggregate principal
amount not to exceed $70,000,000 to provide funds for (a) financing or
refinancing all or a portion of the costs of certain capital expenditures,
including, but not limited to, acquiring, constructing, maintaining,
enlarging, improving, and/or equipping one or more of the following: (1)
golf and tennis facility improvements, (2) football stadium improvements,
and (3) a baseball performance center; (b) paying certain necessary
expenses incidental thereto, including the costs of issuing the Series 2024
Bonds (defined above), and any credit enhancement in connection
therewith (together, (a) and (b) constitute the “Projects”); (c) financing
capitalized interest on the Series 2024 Bonds; and (d) refunding all of the
outstanding Private Colleges and Universities Authority Revenue Bonds
(Mercer University Project), Series 2013 (the “Refunded Bonds”), witha
portion of the proceeds of the Series 2024 Bonds, all as more particularly
described in the Application submitted to the Authority and approved by
the Authority on January 11, 2024; and

The aforementioned Bonds will be issued by the Private Colleges and
Universities Authority, an instrumentality of the State of Georgia, and the
Facilities will be owned and operated by Mercer, which is located entirely
within the boundaries of the State of Georgia; and

The Governor is the chief elected executive officer of the State of Georgia;
and

WHEREAS: This executive order is intended to constitute the approval required by
Section 147(f) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended; and

WHEREAS: A hearing which was open to the public relating to the proposed issuance of
the aforementioned Bonds, was held on January 29, 2024, for which due
and reasonable public notice was given in accordance with the provisions of
law and the procedures established therefor; and

WHEREAS: The Private Colleges and Universities Authority, following such hearing, has
recommended that the issuance of the aforementioned Bonds be approved;
and

WHEREAS: I, as Governor of the State of Georgia, have made a determination to
approve the issuance of the aforementioned Bonds solely for the purpose of
satisfying the requirement for such approval under Section 147(f) of the
Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, as recommended by the
Private Colleges and Universities Authority.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS
GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, PARTICULARLY BY VIRTUE OF THE
PROVISIONS OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE CODE, IT IS HEREBY

ORDERED: The issuance of the aforementioned Bonds by the Private Colleges and
Universities Authority on behalf of the State of Georgia is hereby approved
solely for the purpose of satisfying the requirements for such approval
under Section 147(f) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

The Georgia Department of Community Affairs has been charged with the
responsibility of administering the affairs of the Georgia Housing and Finance
Authority, including the administration of the federal low-income housing tax
credit program in Georgia; and

The Georgia Department of Community Affairs, acting on behalf of the Georgia
Housing and Finance Authority, published two drafts of the 2024-2025 Georgia
Qualified Allocation Plan on the Department’s website on August 9, 2023, and
September 6, 2023, and gave due notice of the availability of the 2024-2025
Georgia Qualified Allocation Plan drafts and of the public hearings on the
Department's public website and through notices sent to industry participants; and

The Georgia Department of Community Affairs held three public hearings
pursuant to due and reasonable notice: one virtual public hearing on August 22,
2023, one hybrid public hearing in Atlanta, Georgia on September 13, 2023, and
one in-person public hearing in Madison, Georgia on September 25, 2023; and

Following the hearings and public comment period, the Board of Directors of the
Georgia Housing and Finance Authority adopted the 2024-2025 Georgia Qualified
Allocation Plan on November 15, 2023.

Now, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS
GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That, solely for the purpose of satisfying the requirements for such approval under
Section 42(m)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code, as amended by the Omnibus
Budget Reconciliation Act of 1989, the 2024-2025 Georgia Qualified Allocation
Plan, in the form approved by the Board of Directors for the Georgia Housing and
Finance Authority on November 15, 2023, is approved.
